title: Streaming decoder for gzip NDJSON files

user_story.i_want: to stream-decode a gzip NDJSON file from S3 line by line
user_story.so_that: large files don't need to fit in memory and one bad line doesn't kill the file

description: The chain is: GetObject, then ByteStream into AsyncRead, then an async-compression gzip decoder, then a BufReader reading lines, then `serde_json::from_str::<IngestedRecord>()` per line. It yields `DecodedLine {line_no, result}`. Lines over 1 MiB and empty lines are handled explicitly. The core function is generic over any `AsyncBufRead + Unpin`, so tests use in-memory bytes. Errors are classified: a corrupt or truncated gzip is fatal (Reject), and a network error mid-stream is retryable (Retry).

acceptance_criteria.then: peak memory stays well below the file size (measurement noted in the PR)
997 records are Ok and 3 errors carry the correct line numbers

rust_concepts: Generic functions over R: AsyncBufRead + Unpin

references.title: The Rust Book ch.17: Async & await
